study_id: Lisboa et al. - 2022 - Enhanced survival prediction using explainable artificial intelligence in heart transplantation

eligibility.Eligibility Rationale: The study analyzes adult heart transplant recipients using a neural network (non‑linear AI) to predict 1‑year mortality, includes relevant outcomes and comparator, and is a peer‑reviewed article published after 2018.

identification_methods.Sponsorship source: Swedish Research Council, Vinnova, Swedish Heart-Lung Foundation, region Skane research funds, donation funds from Skane University Hospital, Anna-Lisa and Sven Eric Lundgrens Foundation
identification_methods.Comments: Retrospective cohort study of heart transplantation using UNOS and Scandinavian registries to develop and externally validate an interpretable self‑explaining neural network (Partial Response Network) against deep learning, IHTSA and IMPACT models.
identification_methods.Institution: Liverpool John Moores University; Lund University
identification_methods.Dataset Source: UNOS SRTR registry and Scandia Thoracic Transplantation Database
identification_methods.Identification Notes: Included adult heart transplant recipients (≥18 y); excluded pediatric cases, donor age <15 y and records with missing mandatory data.
identification_methods.Design: Retrospective Cohort with temporal derivation (1997‑2013), test (2014‑2016) and external blinded validation cohorts (2017‑2018).
identification_methods.AI Model Architecture: Self‑explaining neural network (Partial Response Network) with ANOVA decomposition, Lasso‑regularised GAM; benchmarked against deep learning model and IHTSA/IMPACT.
identification_methods.Class Imbalance: Handled by PRN probabilistic threshold adjustment for class assignment.
identification_methods.Comparator: International Heart Transplant Survival Algorithm (IHTSA), IMPACT score, Explainable Boosting Machines (EBM).
identification_methods.Input Variables: Recipient age, donor age, creatinine, ischemic time, ventilator at OHT, diagnosis (non‑ischemic cardiomyopathy), recipient female gender, infection within 2 weeks, transplant year, plus a two‑way interaction (recipient age × ICM).
identification_methods.Missing Data Handling: Multiple imputation (probability imputation with stratified era) for UNOS data; median imputation for Scandinavian dataset.
identification_methods.Validation Method: Temporal split (derivation, test, external validation); five‑fold cross‑validation for recalibrated IHTSA; external cohorts from UNOS (2017‑2018) and Scandia database.
identification_methods.Methods Notes: Data extracted from UNOS SRTR (1987‑onward) and Scandia registry; ANOVA decomposition to obtain partial responses; Lasso for variable selection; GAM for interpretability; statistical analysis with Stata 16.1, Mann‑Whitney U, chi‑square, Hosmer–Lemeshow, AUROC with DeLong test.

population.Inclusion criteria: Heart transplant recipients from UNOS registry between Jan 1 1987 and Jun 30 2020 meeting mandatory data completeness; adult recipients (≥18 years)
population.Exclusion criteria: Pediatric recipients (<18 years), donor age <15 years, missing mandatory data (age, sex, follow‑up duration, vital status)
population.Population Notes: Three cohorts: derivation (n=31,315), test (n=6,120) and external blinded validation (n=4,750); cohorts differ in age, BMI, comorbidities
population.Diagnosis: Non‑ischemic cardiomyopathy (NICM) most common (60% in validation cohort)

interventions_outcomes.Intervention Input Data Modality: Tabular clinical variables (recipient and donor characteristics, demographics, physiological measurements)
interventions_outcomes.Number of Predictors: 10 (nine univariate effects plus one two‑way interaction)
interventions_outcomes.Feature Selection Method: LASSO (L1 regularisation) applied to partial responses
interventions_outcomes.Temporal Handling: Derivation cohort 1997–2013, test cohort 2014–2016, external blinded validation cohort 2017–2018 (temporal validation)
interventions_outcomes.Interventions Notes: Self‑explaining neural network (PRN) benchmarked against deep learning IHTSA and traditional IMPACT models; external validation on UNOS (n=4750) and Scandinavian (n=2293) datasets.
interventions_outcomes.Outcomes Notes: Primary outcome is classification of death within one year after heart transplantation.
interventions_outcomes.Result data Notes: AUROC for PRN-Lasso in external validation cohort: 0.628 (95% CI 0.602–0.654); comparable to IHTSA (0.635) and superior to IMPACT (0.602).
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome group: Heart transplant recipients in the external blinded validation cohort (UNOS 2017–2018, n = 4750)
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome Metric Definition: Area under the ROC curve calculated on a completely held‑out external validation cohort
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome Notes: PRN‑Lasso achieved similar discrimination to deep learning models while being interpretable and well calibrated.
